industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried, with the tape now agreeing: Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: D now, A prior, the sharpest fall in technology, where last week's reading still ranked the sector B. The two conditions for Neutral (the AI credit channel stabilising; a second house joining Jefferies' European call) could not be tested because no strategist reached the pack; the only artificial-intelligence item is an undated headline that low AI exposure is Europe's edge. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). Of the Pool's semiconductor names, Technoprobe, AT&S, INFICON, Sensirion, STMicroelectronics, Soitec, AIXTRON and AMS Osram are marked leaving the Pool or meet a Sell Criterion, so the row's cost to the Lists is falling of its own accord. Counter-case: demand was never the problem and European exposure is equipment, power and optics. To C when the AI credit channel is read stable or a second house joins the European call, with relative strength holding C or better.

geography.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the Swiss index is among those Goldman (19 Oct) names as rallying alongside non-AI and low-beta exposures, which is the rotation this row was set on; the Swiss National Bank was not re-read this week, so last week's 'not hiking' stands. Relative strength is not graded by country. Counter-case unchanged: the franc takes 2 to 3 points a year off a Swiss exporter's reported profit (Sonova memo), and five of the Swiss Pool names are semiconductor names inside an Underweight sector. Back to C if the SNB joins the hikers or the franc reverses.

memo.verdict: Park. Neutral on the business, bearish on the price at CHF 375.2 (2026-10-06); conviction medium. The record calls COMET a cyclical demand-inflection case with a self-help margin overlay, compelling as a business story and not compelling as an investment at this price, because the market already pays a mid-range multiple (19.6 times consensus 24-month-forward EPS of CHF 19.16) for what consensus expects the peak-cycle year of 2028 to earn; on the framework's convention the modal return is about minus 11 percent a year over eighteen months and minus 4 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar. The case is parked on the return, not by the gate: management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability B, so no D or F sits on the gate. Re-entry conditions named: below about CHF 285 the blend of the record's two branches clears the bar; below about CHF 240 the modal path clears it (about CHF 220 on the adverse drop-through); and at any price, evidence that the 2028 peak is not a peak (customer visibility into 2029; a PCT EBITDA margin above 22 percent by Q4 2026; a FY2027 margin guide above 20 percent) would move the structural branch from possible to plausible and the case from park to progress. Not an invalidation: every one of the ten combination red flags is absent or only partly forming.
case: The change is external, cyclical and of the strongest kind the framework recognises. Wafer-fab-equipment spending is inflecting on AI, 3D memory and gate-all-around logic. The evidence is orders and customer capital spending rather than forecasts: Lam Research raised its 2026 WFE growth forecast to 38 percent from 27 percent, Applied Materials guided 2026 systems shipment growth above 30 percent, front-end makers report visibility into 2027, VAT Group's H1 2026 orders rose 75 percent to CHF 856m with a record CHF 648m backlog, and Comet's own book-to-bill was 1.48 for H1 2026 with Q2 orders up 45 percent on Q1. Industry forecasts run from 10 to 23 percent WFE growth in 2026 and from USD 100bn to nearly USD 170bn by 2030. Half of Comet's exposure is memory, the most cyclical end, and management itself dates the peak to 2028; the record treats the force as cyclical until proven structural. Comet's own cycle turned up from a H1 2024 trough (semi-annual revenue CHF 189m then; CHF 240m in H1 2026) and lags the front-end peers by about a quarter (H1 2026 growth 5.6 percent reported against INFICON's 18 percent).

The internal change is real and multi-dimensional, and it decides how much of the cycle reaches EPS, not whether the cycle arrives. Penang doubles matching-network capacity at a fifth of Swiss labour cost; the efficiency programme is dated 2028; the chair, CFO and two board seats changed within eighteen months; the X-ray perimeter is being cut (Hamburg restructuring; Beijing liquidated; channel partners from 13 to zero); two product platforms (Synertia generators-plus-matches, doubling the addressable market to USD 7.1bn by 2028; the CA20 advanced-packaging X-ray tool with over 25 qualifications) have moved from concept to orders. The screen's three-strong rule is met; the red flags are absent. Not A because the chief executive is unchanged in his fifth year, the mid-term targets were cut in November 2025 (largely currency: USD/CHF 0.70 against 0.90), shareholder returns were cut, and the duplicate-cost period through H2 2026 and 2027 is the execution risk the research keeps returning to.

'Financial Outputs' have turned up at every layer. H1 2026 sales rose 12.7 percent in constant currency; the EBITDA margin rose to 13.1 percent from 10.1 despite CHF 4.5m of one-offs; EBITDA rose CHF 8.4m on CHF 12.6m of extra sales, a 67 percent drop-through; consensus FY2027 EPS is up 41 percent in six months to CHF 14.91. Revenue growth steps from 2.6 percent (FY2025) to about 24 percent (FY2026), 27 to 31 percent (FY2027) and 12 to 17 percent (FY2028) against a three-year history of minus 22 percent cumulative; the margin is the largest single lever (consensus 16.5 / 22.6 / 25.3 percent; the record's path 15.9 / 21.8 / 24.5). Cash is the laggard: H1 2026 free cash flow CHF -19.3m; net working capital 33.8 percent of trailing revenue on FactSet's definition against a target below 20 percent; consignment demands push working capital upstream for the whole upcycle. Further sell-side upgrades are probable over six to twelve months: the record's modal FY2026 (sales about CHF 565m; EBITDA about CHF 90m, 15.9 percent) sits in the upper half of guidance; Deutsche Bank called the outlook "highly cautious given record orders"; the planning currency 0.70 is below spot 0.80; consensus FY2027 margin 22.6 percent sits below what the drop-through record gives. But consensus has already risen 41 percent, consensus FY2028 revenue (CHF 876m) exceeds the top of management's 2028 range (CHF 770m at 0.70; about CHF 858m at the 0.80 spot), coverage is seven brokers, and the upgrade record is D: 2023 sales guided CHF 440m to CHF 480m, delivered CHF 397.5m; the 2024 margin guided 15 to 17 percent, delivered 13.6; the 2025 margin guided 17 to 20 percent, cut to 10 to 14; four of five windows missed or reset. Modal EPS growth sits far above the 12 to 20 percent band at every horizon (about 125 percent a year FY2025 to FY2028), which the framework marks down for over-extrapolation; in a 'Demand Inflection' case the inflection is the point, but the sell-side is already extrapolating it.
counter_case: The strongest case against is the sell-side's, in its strongest form, and the record carries it at full force. Consensus is still too low and the multiple is too low with it. Deutsche Bank sits 29 to 31 percent above consensus on 2027 and 2028 EBITDA and carries FY2028 EPS of CHF 24.62 against the median CHF 20.10 (UBS CHF 24.01), because consensus under-counts the Penang saving, the efficiency programme and Synertia's conversion of 100-plus engagements. The FY2026 guide is set to be beaten: the midpoint implies an H2 2026 run-rate of CHF 315m and the H1 book-to-bill of 1.48 supports more; the H1 intake built about CHF 115m of backlog; Deutsche Bank keeps CHF 580m and a 17.8 percent margin against a guide it calls "highly cautious given record orders". The planning currency of 0.70 against spot near 0.80 is a built-in upgrade, "significantly more conservative than peer baselines" (VAT at 0.83). The AI-driven cycle is structural, not cyclical: WFE from USD 100bn to USD 170bn by 2030, over 70 new fabs, gate-all-around and 3D DRAM intensity multiplying etch and deposition steps, so there is no 2030 down-leg to look through and the framework's convention is valuing a dip that will not happen. Penang and the efficiency programme lift the margin to 25 to 28 percent, above the last peak, which is why the trough-multiple history is the wrong anchor: the next trough is a different company. At 19.6 times Comet is the cheapest equipment name in its sector at a 40 to 45 percent discount to VAT against a historical 20 percent; as upgrades arrive it re-rates towards the sector median of 25 times. At 25.3 times on CHF 19.16 the shares are worth CHF 485 within twelve to eighteen months, where the consensus target sits (CHF 483 to CHF 500, itself a 20 percent-plus return); at 25 times on a raised FY2028 EPS of CHF 24 they are worth CHF 600, a 35 percent-plus annual return. The evidence for it is real: the H1 2026 drop-through, the order book, the Lam upgrade, the brokers' upward march on every line at three and six months, the two highest FY2028 estimates. On the record's own arithmetic, the structural branch at the median multiple returns about plus 16 percent a year and at the "defendable" band plus 25 percent a year, and the blend of the record's own branches returns zero: the shares are fairly priced for the odds the record itself assigns.

A second counter-case, at Building Block 2: the record is grading a trough. The ratios it leans on (ROCE 5.2 percent; a 10.1 percent margin) come from a picture drawn before the H1 2026 results, whereas the H1 2026 results show the PCT margin at 20.2 percent and a cost base about to halve in labour terms; on that view the franchise (competitors buy the product; a two-player capacitor market; qualification lock-in) deserves a B and the trough numbers are noise. A third, at Building Block 3: the crisp pattern is the wrong one; this is a 'Major Corporate Change' case (Penang, the efficiency programme, Synertia, the CA20, a refreshed board), and pricing a self-help story as a cycle understates the structural margin gain and looks through a 2030 dip the new cost base would prevent. A fourth, at Building Block 4: the valuation has leaked into a Building Block meant to judge shape, and on shape alone (clear mechanism, absent red flags, A-grade momentum and estimate direction, three key drivers, a narrow perimeter) this is a B.
triggers: - Invalidate (downwards): a Lam or Applied WFE guide cut above 15 percent; Comet's book-to-bill below 1.0 for two consecutive quarters by Q1 2027; any OEM acquisition of an RF subsystem supplier; Synertia revenue short of CHF 50m by 2027.

- Alarm (downwards): a PCT EBITDA margin below 22 percent by Q4 2026 despite rising sales (Penang not delivering); book-to-bill below 1.0 in a quarter; a memory-price reversal; Lam's share of sales falling while WFE rises; CA20 orders below 15 units by end-2026; a European semiconductor-hardware de-rating like July 2026's; a change of voice at Deutsche Bank.

- Upwards, from park to progress: customers' 2027 outlooks extending the up-leg into 2029; management dropping "peak" from its 2028 language; a FY2027 margin guide above 20 percent on 2027-03-11; the PCT margin above 22 percent by Q4 2026; peers holding their multiples through 2027 while estimates rise.
- Price triggers: below about CHF 285 the blend clears the bar; below about CHF 240 the modal path clears it (CHF 220 on the adverse drop-through; CHF 190 over three years).

- Dated steps: Penang start of production late 2026; the Lam, Applied and Tokyo Electron calendar-2027 outlooks; FY2026 results and the FY2027 guide on 2027-03-11; the H1 2027 results as the first full Penang-cost half; the Flamatt wind-down and the efficiency programme's completion by end-2027; the 2028 peak targets.

- Open on the evidence: whether the cycle is structural into 2030 (the record: 60 percent cyclical, 40 percent structural); whether the tax rate settles near 20 percent or the Malaysian shift lowers it to 17 (the one transmission link the record cannot name with confidence); whether the Penang saving makes the next trough margin materially higher than the last; the true capacitor share (70 or 50 percent); whether VAT's front-loaded 2027 orders reflect over-ordering; the store's TSR/Valuation re-basing to the stated 'Modal return' (expected D or F).
